*Source*: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) – “DEC Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Plants” PDF (published 20 Nov 2020, revised from the 2014 regulation).  
*Body that keeps the record*: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.  
*Term used for the list*: “Prohibited” (plants which cannot be possessed, sold, imported, etc.).  
*Dataset start year (first publication of the list)*: 2014 (regulation, updated in 2020).

**Plants listed as “Prohibited”**

*Terrestrials*  
- Amur Cork Tree (Phellodendron amurense)  
- Amur Honeysuckle (Lonicera maackii)  
- Autumn Olive (Elaeagnus umbellata)  
- Beach Vitex (Vitex rotundifolia)  
- Black Swallow‑wort (Cynanchum louiseae) (also listed as *C. nigrum, Vincetoxicum nigrum*)  
- Bohemian Knotweed (Reynoutria x bohemica) (also *Fallopia x bohemica, Polygonum x bohemica*)  
- Border Privet (Ligustrum obtusifolium)  
- Broad‑leaf Pepper‑grass (Lepidium latifolium)  
- Canada Thistle (Cirsium arvense) (including *C. setosum, C. incanum, Serratula arvensis*)  
- Chinese Lespedeza (Lespedeza cuneata)  
- Chinese Yam (Dioscorea polystachya) (also *D. batatas*)  
- Cogon Grass (Imperata cylindrica) (also *I. arundinacea, Lagurus cylindricus*)  
- Common Buckthorn (Rhamnus cathartica)  
- Cup‑plant (Silphium perfoliatum)  
- Cut‑leaf Teasel (Dipsacus laciniatus)  
- Cypress Spurge (Euphorbia cyparissias)  
- Fly Honeysuckle (Lonicera x bella)  
- Garden Loosestrife (Lysimachia vulgaris)  
- Garlic Mustard (Alliaria petiolata)  
- Giant Hogweed (Heracleum mantegazzianum)  
- Giant Knotweed (Reynoutria sachalinensis) (also *Fallopia sachalinensis, Polygonum sachalinensis*)  
- Golden Bamboo (Phyllostachys aurea)  
- Gray Florist’s Willow (Salix atrocinerea)  
- Japanese Angelica Tree (Aralia elata)  
- Japanese Barberry (Berberis thunbergii)  
- Japanese Chaff Flower (Achyranthes japonica)  
- Japanese Honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica)  
- Japanese Hops (Humulus japonicus)  
- Japanese Knotweed (Reynoutria japonica) (also *Fallopia japonica, Polygonum cuspidatum*)  
- Japanese Stilt Grass (Microstegium vimineum)  
- Japanese Virgin’s Bower (Clematis ternifora)  
- Kudzu (Pueraria montana)  
- Leafy Spurge (Euphorbia esula)  
- Lesser Celandine (Ficaria verna) (also *Ranunculus fcaria*)  
- Mile‑a‑minute Weed (Persicaria perfoliata) (also *Polygonum perfoliatum*)  
- Morrow’s Honeysuckle (Lonicera morrowii)  
- Multifora Rose (Rosa multifora)  
- Pale Swallow‑wort (Cynanchum rossicum) (also *C. medium, Vincetoxicum medium, V. rossicum*)  
- Porcelain Berry (Ampelopsis brevipedunculata)  
- Slender False Brome (Brachypodium sylvaticum)  
- Small Carpetgrass (Arthraxon hispidus)  
- Spotted Knapweed (Centauria stoebe) (also *C. biebersteinii, C. diffusa, C. maculosa misapplied, C. xpsammogena*)  
- Sycamore Maple (Acer pseudoplatanus)  
- Tartarian Honeysuckle (Lonicera tatarica)  
- Wavyleaf Basketgrass (Oplismenus hirtellus)  
- Wild Chervil (Anthriscus sylvestris)  
- Wineberry (Rubus phoenicolasius)  
- Yellow Groove Bamboo (Phyllostachys aureosulcata)

*Wet‑land*  
- Common Reed Grass (Phragmites australis)  
- Marsh Dewfower (Murdannia keisak)  
- Purple Loosestrife (Lythrum salicaria)  
- Reed Manna Grass (Glyceria maxima)  
- Smooth Buckthorn (Frangula alnus) (also *Rhamnus frangula*)  
- Yellow Iris (Iris pseudacorus)

*Aquatic*  
- Brazilian Waterweed (Egeria densa)  
- Broadleaf Water‑milfoil (Hybrid Myriophyllum heterophyllum × M. laxum)  
- Curly Pondweed (Potamogeton crispus)  
- Eurasian Water‑milfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum)  
- Fanwort (Cabomba caroliniana)  
- Floating Primrose Willow (Ludwigia peploides)  
- Frogbit (Hydrocharis morsus‑ranae)  
- Hydrilla/Water Thyme (Hydrilla verticillata)  
- Parrot‑feather (Myriophyllum aquaticum)  
- Uruguayan Primrose Willow (Ludwigia hexapetala) (also *L. grandifora*)  
- Water Chestnut (Trapa natans)  
- Yellow Floating Heart (Nymphoides peltata)

I located the official New York State Department of Environmental Conservation PDF that contains the full list of prohibited and regulated invasive plants (Publication date: 20 Nov 2020). The document is titled **“New York State Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Plants”** and is found at:
<https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/docs/lands_forests_pdf/isprohibitedplants2.pdf>  

The PDF is organized into plant categories—Terrestrial, Wetland, Aquatic, (and Regulated) groups—with each entry listing both the common name and scientific name. The list is extensive (more than 100 species) and includes entries such as:
- *Amur Cork Tree* (Phellodendron amurense)
- *Japanese Honeysuckle* (Lonicera japonica)
- *Giant Hogweed* (Heracleum mantegazzianum)
- *Mile‑a‑minute Weed* (Persicaria perfoliata)
- *Brazilian Waterweed* (Egeria densa)
- *Common Reed Grass* (Phragmites australis)
- *Japanese Barberry* (Berberis thunbergii)
- *Cypress Spurge* (Euphorbia cyparissias)
- *Wild Chervil* (Anthriscus sylvestris)
- *Japanese Knotweed* (Reynoutria japonica)
- *Black Swallow‑wort* (Cynanchum louiseae)  

The PDF also contains “Regulated” species that can be legally possessed but not introduced.

The information I could extract from the PDF via browsing included full listings for several categories, but not every entry; the PDF itself is the definitive source for the complete, up‑to‑date list. A more recent version of the list may be available; the current PDF’s publication year is 2020.

information:
- The page is the New York State (DEC) “Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Plants” list, published in the NYCRR Part 575, issued 20 Nov 2020 (PDF: `https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/docs/lands_forests_pdf/isprohibitedplants2.pdf`).  
- It contains the full list of federally and state‑level prohibited invasive plant species, divided into three categories:  
  1. **Terrestrial plants** – e.g., *Amur Cork Tree (Phellodendron amurense)*, *Japanese Barberry (Berberis thunbergii)*, *Giant Hogweed (Heracleum mantegazzianum)*, *Japanese Knotweed (Reynoutria japonica)*, etc.  
  2. **Wetland plants** – e.g., *Phragmites australis* (common reed), *Lythrum salicaria* (purple loosestrife), *Frangula alnus* (smooth buckthorn), etc.  
  3. **Aquatic plants** – e.g., *Egeria densa* (Brazilian waterweed), *Myriophyllum spicatum* (eurasian water‑milfoil), *Trapa natans* (water chestnut), etc.  
- The PDF lists each species with its common name, scientific name, and page reference.  
- The list is used by the New York Department of Environmental Conservation in enforcement and regulation of invasive species.

The PDF at https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/docs/lands_forests_pdf/isprohibitedplants2.pdf is the official “New York State Prohibited and Regulated Invasive Plants” list published by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC). It contains the complete list of prohibited species, organized by category (Terrestrial, Wetland, Aquatic). The regulation was promulgated on September 10 2014 (effective 6 months later) and the PDF itself was last updated on 20 November 2020. The document lists all prohibited (and regulated) invasive plants; the prohibited list contains 69 species. No further information is required to locate the list or understand its scope.
